title: DDLumos: Understanding and Detecting Atomic DDL Bugs in DBMSs
problem: Database management systems have bugs where DDL (Data Definition Language) operations fail to maintain atomicity, leaving databases in inconsistent states. Current DBMSs lack systematic understanding and detection mechanisms for these atomic DDL violations.
motivation: Atomic guarantees for DDL operations are fundamental to database consistency; undetected atomicity bugs in production databases can cause silent data corruption and system failures.
method: DDLumos systematically analyzes atomicity violations in DDL operations through specification-based testing, generating DDL operation sequences to expose failure modes. It combines dynamic analysis with transaction state monitoring to detect inconsistencies when DDL operations partially fail or interleave with concurrent operations.
key_novelty: Systematic characterization and automated detection of atomic DDL bug patterns across different DBMS implementations using a unified testing framework.
contributions: Taxonomy of atomic DDL bug categories and failure modes in production databases
DDLumos detection tool that automatically identifies atomicity violations in DDL operations
Empirical study revealing previously unknown atomicity bugs in PostgreSQL, MySQL, and other major DBMSs

metrics.other: number of bugs detected, false positive rate, detection coverage

limitations: Not discussed in title only; specific DBMS coverage and scope of atomic operations analyzed unknown.
